[[File:Iwa-jinja (Kashiwara), torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]

'''Iwa Shrine''' (石神社) is a Shinto shrine located in Taiheiji, Kashiwara City, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former shrine Rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}.

==Enshrined Deities==
; Main Deity
* {{ill|Princess Ishi-hime|en|Princess Ishi-hime|qid=Q11585498|lt=Ishihime Hime}} – the imperial princess of {{ill|Emperor Senka|en|Emperor Senka|qid=Q329728|lt=Emperor Senga}} and the empress of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}}.

; Auxiliary Deities
* {{ill|Iwanaga-hime|en|Iwanaga-hime|qid=Q8191705|lt=Ishinagahime}}
* {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現}}

==Overview==
The shrine is situated on the hillside of a small elevated hill near the southern end of the {{ill|Ikoma Mountains|ja|生駒山地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Mountain Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11574917}} in the Taiheiji area of Kashiwara City. An office is located at the foot of the precincts, while the main hall stands atop a flight of high stone steps. According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}, in the 9th year of the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan}} era (February {{ill|867|en|867|qid=Q30347|lt=867}}) it was listed as an official shrine, and in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinja Meicho|ja|延喜式神名帳}} it is classified as a small shrine. In the Edo period, it was revered as the guardian deity of Taiheiji Village and was known as Kumano Gongen Shrine. In ancient times, there was a temple in this area known as {{ill|Chishiki-ji|ja|知識寺|lt=Chishikiji|lt_ja=智識寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chishikiji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 智識寺跡|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11584664}}. It is said that {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|en|Emperor Shōmu|qid=Q349263|lt=Emperor Shōmu}} and {{ill|Empress Kōken|en|Empress Kōken|qid=Q232955|lt=Emperor Kōken}} visited this temple during their travels between {{ill|Naniwa Palace|ja|難波宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naniwa Palace|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3608523}} and {{ill|Heijō Palace|en|Heijō Palace|qid=Q211585|lt=Heijō Palace}}, performing worship rituals. At Chishikiji, a large {{ill|Birushana Buddha|ja|毘盧遮那仏|lt=Rurashina Buddha|lt_ja=廬舎那仏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rurashina Buddha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17193861}} was enshrined; upon beholding it, Emperor Shōmu is said to have initiated the construction of the {{ill|Great Buddha of Tōdaiji|ja|東大寺大仏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東大寺盧舎那仏像|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11526469}}. Later, Chishikiji fell into decline around the Muromachi period.

==Precincts==
Within the precincts stands a large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|ab|Акамфараҵла|af|Kanferboom|an|Cinnamomum camphora|ar|كافور (نبات)|arz|كافور (نبات)|ast|Cinnamomum camphora|az|Camphora officinarum|be|Камфоравае дрэва|bg|Камфорово дърво|bn|কর্পূর গাছ|ca|Camforer|ceb|Dalapot|cs|Kafrovník lékařský|da|Kamfertræ|de|Kampferbaum|dv|ކާފޫރު ގަސް|eo|Kamforarbo|es|Cinnamomum camphora|eu|Kanforrondo|fa|درخت کافور|fi|Kamferipuu|fr|Camphrier|frr|Kamferbuum|gl|Alcanforeiro|hi|कपूर|hr|Kamforovo drvo|hsb|Kamferowy štom|hu|Kámforfa|hy|Կամֆորայի ծառ|id|Camphora officinarum|it|Cinnamomum camphora|ja|クスノキ|ka|ქაფურის ხე|kk|Камфора ағашы|kn|ಕರ್ಪೂರ ಮರ|ko|녹나무|ku|Dara kamfûrê|la|Cinnamomum camphora|mg|Camphora officinarum|ml|കർപ്പൂരം|ms|Kapur tohori|my|ပရုတ်ပင်|ne|कपुरको रूख|nl|Kamferboom|nn|Kamfertre|no|Kamfertre|oc|Camfrièr|or|କର୍ପୁର|pa|ਕਪੂਰ (ਦਰੱਖ਼ਤ)|pl|Cynamonowiec kamforowy|pt|Cinnamomum camphora|pwn|drakes|qu|Alkachu|ru|Коричник камфорный|sl|Kafrovec|sv|Kamferträd|ta|கற்பூர மரம்|te|సిన్నామోనం కాంఫొర|th|การบูร (พรรณไม้)|tr|Kâfur ağacı|uk|Камфорне дерево|vi|Long não (cây)|war|Cinnamomum camphora|za|Gaucah|zh|樟树|zh_min_nan|Chiuⁿ-á|zh_yue|樟|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor Tree}}, a massive tree with an approximate circumference of 6 meters and a height exceeding 16 meters. It is estimated to be 700–800 years old and has been designated a Natural Monument by Osaka Prefecture.

Next to the shrine office within the precincts is the foundation stone of the east tower of Chishikiji, which has been designated as a cultural property by Osaka Prefecture. The column hole of this foundation stone has a diameter of 122 cm and was once used as the shrine’s hand-washing stone, although it is now enclosed by a fence.

==Festivals==
* Summer Grand Festival (July 18, 19)  
The festival, known as the "Orei-sai," is held on the second Saturday and Sunday of July (mid-July). During this event, the Taiheiji area offers magnificent futon drums. The futon drums feature carvings by the renowned Banshu craftsman, Kuroda Masakatsu, the third in his lineage.
* Annual Festival (Autumn Festival) (October 19)

==Cultural Properties==
=== Cultural Properties Designated by Osaka Prefecture ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties  
** The foundation stone of the east tower pillar of Chishikiji (archaeological material) – owned by Iwa Shrine. Designated on February 20, 1970<ref>[http://www.city.kashiwara.osaka.jp/docs/2014082200096/?doc_id=1500 The foundation stone of the east tower pillar of Chishikiji] (Kashiwara City website).</ref>
* Natural Monuments  
** The camphor tree of Iwa Shrine – designated on August 4, 1978<ref>[http://www.city.kashiwara.osaka.jp/docs/2014082200232/?doc_id=1514 The camphor tree of Iwa Shrine] (Kashiwara City website).</ref>

==Visitor Information==
; Location
* {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|Kashiwara|en|Kashiwara|qid=Q873583|lt=Kashiwara City}} Taiheiji 2-19-13

; Access
* Railway: Alight at {{ill|Osaka Line|en|Osaka Line|qid=Q1052545|lt=Kintetsu Osaka Line}} and {{ill|Andō Station|en|Andō Station|qid=Q4761545|lt=Ando Station}}, then walk approximately 10 minutes (about 800 m east)

; Surroundings
The path leading north in front of the shrine is part of an ancient route that ran north–south along the foothills of the Ikoma Mountains even before the establishment of the {{ill|Higashi Kōya Kaidō|ja|東高野街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitakano Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11528777}}. It is said that {{ill|Ariwara no Narihira|en|Ariwara no Narihira|qid=Q451991|lt=Ariwara no Narihira}} once traversed this route between {{ill|Hiraoka Shrine|en|Hiraoka Shrine|qid=Q32422|lt=Hiraoka Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato and Kawachi provinces.
